The full question asks whether, for every finite order n, radial convexity of d_f(A,B)=||f(A)-f(B)||_F on positive definite n-by-n matrices is equivalent to matrix monotonicity of degree n (either increasing or decreasing). The paper proves the differentiable order-two case. Its higher-order necessary Hadamard-square condition does not yield the desired positivity by a pointwise matrix argument. A

For C1 f, diagonalize A=diag(lambda_i); the derivative T_A=Df(A) is the real self-adjoint Schur multiplier with Loewner matrix L_ij=f[1](lambda_i,lambda_j), diagonal f'(lambda_i). Loewner's fixed-degree criterion says that L>=0 for every node tuple is equivalent to increasing matrix monotonicity of that same degree. This criterion does not allow replacing L by its Hadamard square.

More generally, let an old plane rooted tree have N edges and all original leaf delays <=d. Attach a new path of a edges as an *exterior root branch*, on either side, giving its unique original leaf delay d. Any legal enlarged order has at least d-1 old removals before its first new-path removal. Before that point old and global positions agree. Thereafter every old release has already occurred. R

If d>N+1 no shuffle is possible. Otherwise the shuffle weight is G(N+a-d+1,a) for a left exterior branch, and q^(a(d-1)) G(N+a-d+1,a) for a right exterior branch. The old-order exponent is unchanged; all new/old pairs are incomparable, on a fixed side. Thus these factors multiply Q_old exactly, for arbitrary old trees under the stated maximal-release condition.

Proof of the identity: all new twig vertices must precede p. In an old order with p at position t, the initial d-1 old vertices must precede the first twig removal. This requires t>=d. The remaining t-d old vertices before p can be shuffled freely with the a twig vertices. This contributes the Gaussian.
